jurisdictions.name: India
jurisdictions.law: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023
jurisdictions.maxPenalty: Up to ₹10 lakh per contravention, ₹50 lakh for each later one (s 21). Criminal: up to 2 years and ₹10 lakh, or 5 years and ₹50 lakh for repeat offences (s 89).
jurisdictions.penaltyHeadline: Up to ₹50 lakh + jail for repeat offences

jurisdictions.name: Singapore
jurisdictions.law: Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act (CPFTA) and the CCCS Guidelines on Price Transparency (2020)
jurisdictions.regulator: Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS)
jurisdictions.maxPenalty: CCCS obtains court declarations and injunctions; breaching an injunction can lead to court-ordered fines or jail. Consumers can also claim compensation.
jurisdictions.penaltyHeadline: Court orders; breaches can mean fines or jail

drip_pricing.clause: Drip pricing: unavoidable charges must be in the headline price or shown clearly beside it

subscription_trap.clause: s 4 unfair practice (misleading consumers into recurring subscriptions)

false_urgency.clause: s 4 unfair practice (time-limited offers that are not)

general.clause: s 4 unfair practice (saying or doing anything that may deceive or mislead a consumer)

precedents.summary: Shoppers buying shoes were signed up to a monthly membership disclosed only in fine print.

precedents.outcome: Undertaking to stop misleading time-limited sales
precedents.summary: "Closing down" and "fire sale" ads ran with no end date, implying a short-lived price benefit.

jurisdictions.name: United Kingdom
jurisdictions.law: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 (Part 4) and the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013
jurisdictions.maxPenalty: The CMA can fine directly: up to 10% of global turnover (or £300,000), plus daily penalties and consumer redress orders.

drip_pricing.source: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024
drip_pricing.clause: s 230: an invitation to purchase must show the total price, including mandatory fees

basket_sneaking.clause: reg 40: no extra payment without express consent; pre-ticked boxes do not count

subscription_trap.clause: reg 40: no extra payment without express consent; pre-ticked boxes do not count

false_urgency.source: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024
false_urgency.clause: Sch. 20 banned practices (false limited-time claims); s 226 misleading actions

interface_interference.source: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024

confirm_shaming.source: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024

misleading_price.source: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024

general.source: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024

precedents.summary: Nearly 40,000 customers were opted into paid recycling and unpacking services through pre-ticked boxes.

precedents.outcome: Infringement notice and about £760,000 in consumer redress
precedents.summary: The CMA’s first infringement decision under the new regime, over fees not shown upfront.

jurisdictions.name: European Union
jurisdictions.law: Unfair Commercial Practices Directive, Consumer Rights Directive, Price Indication Directive and Digital Services Act
jurisdictions.regulator: National consumer authorities; European Commission for the DSA
jurisdictions.maxPenalty: Widespread consumer-law infringements: at least 4% of annual turnover or €2 million. DSA: up to 6% of worldwide annual turnover.

false_urgency.clause: Annex I, point 7: false “very limited time” claims are banned outright

drip_pricing.clause: Art. 7(4)(c): price including taxes and delivery charges

basket_sneaking.clause: Art. 22: express consent for extra payments; no pre-ticked boxes

subscription_trap.clause: Art. 22: express consent for extra payments; no pre-ticked boxes

interface_interference.clause: Art. 25: online interfaces must not deceive or manipulate users

confirm_shaming.clause: Art. 25: online interfaces must not deceive or manipulate users

misleading_price.clause: Art. 6a: a discount must refer to the lowest price of the prior 30 days

general.clause: Art. 5: general prohibition of unfair commercial practices

precedents.summary: The first DSA fine. It included an Art. 25 deceptive-design breach: a “verified” checkmark anyone could buy.

jurisdictions.name: United States
jurisdictions.law: FTC Act §5, Restore Online Shoppers’ Confidence Act (ROSCA) and the FTC Guides Against Deceptive Pricing
jurisdictions.maxPenalty: Injunctions, consumer refunds, and civil penalties per violation for ROSCA and other rule breaches.

subscription_trap.clause: Clear disclosure and express informed consent before charging

misleading_price.clause: 16 CFR §233.1: former price comparisons must reflect a genuine prior price

general.clause: Unfair or deceptive acts or practices

precedents.outcome: $2.5 billion ($1B civil penalty and $1.5B in refunds)
precedents.summary: Shoppers were enrolled in Prime without clear consent, and cancelling was made hard.

jurisdictions.name: South Korea
jurisdictions.law: Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce (amended, in force 14 Feb 2025)
jurisdictions.maxPenalty: Corrective orders, administrative fines (reported at ₩1–5 million per breach) and business suspension of up to 12 months.

drip_pricing.clause: Dark-pattern rule: gradual disclosure of costs

subscription_trap.source: Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce (amended, in force 14 Feb 2025)
subscription_trap.clause: Art. 13(6) hidden renewals; pre-selection of purchase options

interface_interference.source: Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce (amended, in force 14 Feb 2025)

general.source: Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce (amended, in force 14 Feb 2025)
general.clause: Art. 21(1)(i): deceptive or unfair means of inducing consumers

jurisdictions.name: Australia
jurisdictions.law: Australian Consumer Law (Competition and Consumer Act 2010, Sch. 2)
jurisdictions.maxPenalty: Unfair trading practices (from 1 Jul 2027): the greater of A$100 million, 3× the benefit gained, or 30% of adjusted turnover.
jurisdictions.penaltyHeadline: Up to A$100M or 30% of turnover (from Jul 2027)

upcoming.law: Unfair Trading Practices ban (ACL s 28B) and transaction-charge disclosure (s 48A)
upcoming.summary: Bans design that manipulates or unreasonably distorts consumer decisions, and adds drip-pricing and subscription rules.

drip_pricing.clause: s 48 single price (s 48A transaction-based charges from 1 Jul 2027)

misleading_price.clause: s 29 false or misleading representations about price

general.clause: s 18 misleading or deceptive conduct (s 28B unfair trading practices from 1 Jul 2027)
